problem: Autonomous outreach was terminal on sent/provider acknowledgement and did not yet canonically ingest Gmail replies into suppression, follow-up, sales outcome and revenue learning.
root_cause: The working Gmail connector lived in the canonical connected-app execution path while a new server-side Composio attempt had no matching Gmail connection.
The first standalone reply cron therefore created a parallel execution path and failed provider auth.
The existing cycle engine treats a sales action cycle as strictly monotonic and rejected a second FK-bound outcome after the sent outcome had already closed the cycle.
fix: Integrated reply processing into the existing Powerhouse Growth & Revenue OS owner instead of adding another active automation.
Added canonical reply evidence in public.powerhouse_email_reply_events keyed by Gmail provider message ID.
Added public.powerhouse_email_contact_suppressions plus a write-time suppression guard for autonomous email.
Preserved origin action lineage in reply_events.action_id and outcome evidence without weakening the strict cycle-stage guard.
prevention: Never stop commercial email lineage at sent.
Never introduce a second Gmail reply scheduler/CRM/reply store when the canonical Growth & Revenue OS owner can ingest replies.
Enforce provider-message-id idempotency before any reply side effect.
Apply suppression before outbound provider mutation.
Do not weaken cycle-stage validation to attach later replies; preserve origin lineage in evidence when the original cycle is already terminal.
Optimize variants primarily on realized revenue and paid orders, not reply volume.
